summary.intent: Run a new round of load tests against the staging environment to assess whether recent API changes caused performance regressions, then investigate and resolve any root causes found.
summary.outcome: Identified a ~50% upload throughput regression caused by Kubo reprovider CPU contention (76k announced CIDs consuming ~50% of the 1-core cap); validated fixes via A/B/C/D load test runs; landed a PR bumping Kubo 0.40→0.42, setting Provide.Strategy=roots, raising ipfs cpus 1.0→1.5 and memory 2G→3G, and adding an idempotent init script.

repo: All load-test scenarios already use the full SDK (CipherBoxClient), not raw API endpoints — client-pool.ts provisions real accounts via createTestAccount, then drives high-level client methods
Kubo 0.40+ deprecates the entire `Reprovider.*` config block in favor of `Provide.*`; presence of `Reprovider` causes a FATAL on boot (not a warning)
someguy is a read-side delegated-routing proxy only — it cannot accept provider writes/announcements; Fix 2 (delegate providing to someguy) is architecturally infeasible
someguy is called synchronously on the upload critical path via the API's IPNS operations, consuming 30–85% of its 1-core cap during upload load tests
IPNS publish to someguy is fire-and-forget: DB upsert happens first, then delegatedRouting.publish() runs as a detached promise — API response never blocks on DHT propagation
The drift metric cipherbox_drift_orphaned_pins_total is a COUNTER (not a gauge) — it increments once per orphan per hourly drift run and never resets except on container restart
365 @example.com test accounts (load-test harness pattern: `${prefix}-${label}-${Date.now()}@example.com`) hold ~16k of 17.9k pinned CIDs (~90% of the provide workload)
31 missing pins (DB rows with no Kubo pin) belong to 3 dev/owner test accounts — no third-party data loss; mechanism is stale pinned_cids rows surviving after Kubo lost the pin
deploy-staging.yml uses an explicit file list for scp — new files (e.g., docker/ipfs-init/) must be explicitly added or they won't reach the VPS
The CAPACITY.md '4 vCPU baseline' was a doc error — the staging box has always been 2 vCPU / 8 GB; the Phase 19.2 baseline was on this same hardware
Kubo v0.42.0 pinner-lock fix directly benefits Provide.Strategy=roots: reprovide cycle no longer holds a read lock that blocks concurrent pin/add operations
Kubo v0.41 does an irreversible provider-keystore relocation on first boot — volume snapshot required before upgrading

moveItem is the real tail latency hotspot in mixed-workload (p95 9.1s → 42.3s from 50→100 clients) because it triggers two folder-metadata updates + two IPNS publishes; currently ungated in thresholds

code.finding: Pin timer wraps exactly one call — ipfsProvider.pinFile(file.buffer). No delegated-routing or DHT-provide call is made synchronously; Kubo's background reprovider handles announcement after add returns
pinFile makes a single blocking HTTP POST to local Kubo: /api/v0/add?pin=true&cid-version=1. No someguy call on this path
IPNS publish is fire-and-forget: DB upsert first, then delegatedRouting.publish() runs as a detached .then/.catch promise. API response never waits on DHT propagation
IPNS resolve IS synchronously awaited on GET /ipns/resolve, but it is DB-cache-backed — falls through to Postgres-cached CID on BAD_GATEWAY
deleteAccount properly fetches pinned CIDs, calls ipfsProvider.unpinFile(cid) best-effort, then userRepository.delete(userId). Raw SQL deletes would orphan Kubo pins
maxRetries=3, requestTimeoutMs=5000ms per attempt, baseDelayMs=500ms — worst case before fallback: ~16.5s of primary retries before delegated-ipfs.dev fallback
Columns are user_id, cid, size_bytes, pinned_at. No BYO flag — BYO status lives on vaults.is_byo_user joined via user_id=owner_id
Test accounts created as `${prefix}-${label}-${Date.now()}@example.com` — all @example.com emails are safe to bulk-delete as test-harness artifacts
createFolder threshold is hardcoded 5000ms — too tight for 50+ client staging runs (fails at 5034ms with 0 errors); moveItem has no threshold despite being the slowest operation (p95 9–42s)

workflow: `docker update --cpus X <container>` applies CPU cap changes live to a running container without restart — avoids triggering Kubo's provide catch-up settle period
Docker CPU limits are ceilings not reservations; sum of limits can exceed physical cores. Throughput ceiling is the physical core count when both services saturate simultaneously
Throttling a required upstream service (someguy) to free CPU for the caller (Kubo) backfires if the upstream is on the critical path — Run D proved this: someguy@0.4 degraded upload throughput
GC removes unpinned blocks but does not fix reprovider CPU contention — empirically validated (294k→20k objects, zero throughput improvement)
`docker compose exec -T` drains heredoc stdin, swallowing the rest of remote scripts. Fix: append `</dev/null` to each exec call
Single-pin-at-idle test (~18ms) is the clean isolator for 'per-pin cost vs CPU-queuing': fast at idle confirms contention under load, not pinset size
`ipfs stats reprovide` exposes the active provider worker pool and scheduled-CIDs count — decisive for diagnosing reprovider CPU saturation
Kubo RepoVersion=18 in both v0.40.0 and v0.42.0; no one-way repo migration across the jump. Verify with `version.go` before any Kubo upgrade
markdownlint pre-commit hook runs on `.md` files — run `markdownlint --fix` locally before staging docs changes to avoid commit failures

friction: Caused a staging IPFS crash-loop by setting `Reprovider.Strategy` (deprecated) instead of `Provide.Strategy` (correct for Kubo 0.40+) — required emergency config edit to recover
SSH sessions repeatedly confused two VPS IPs: Tailscale node 100.118.33.115 (openclaw-hostinger, unrelated) vs actual staging box 76.13.151.200 — delayed diagnosis
Falsely diagnosed block-garbage bloat as the primary cause with high confidence, then GC empirically refuted it — wasted a GC run + post-GC load test before pivoting
False 'deleted accounts' hypothesis for missing-pin owners due to query bug (users.email column doesn't exist; identity is in auth_methods.identifier_display)
SQL camelCase columns (users.createdAt, auth_methods.userId) require double-quotes in raw psql; caused multiple failed queries
zsh doesn't word-split unquoted `$FILES` variable — broke perl/sed bulk substitution; required explicit loop
Background process launched via `nohup ... &` is not harness-tracked — required a separate harness-tracked until-loop waiter to get notifications
Issue #547 initially referenced uncommitted scratch files (scripts/staging-loadtest-sweep.sh, loadtest-staging-2026-06-22/) — caught by user, required patch
CAPACITY.md contained a bogus '4 vCPU baseline' that caused multiple incorrect diagnoses ('box was downsized') before confirming via Hostinger plan page that it was always 2 vCPU
SSH timeouts occurred mid-session requiring blind retries without clear root cause
open_items: GitHub issue #547: enable periodic Kubo GC — must implement reconcile step (re-pin or prune stale pinned_cids rows) before automating GC, otherwise auto-GC finalizes 'missing' pin drift
Extend drift-report to detect 'missing' direction (DB row with no Kubo pin) and add auto-repair path — currently drift-report is read-only and only tracks orphan direction
Delete 365 @example.com test accounts via proper API path (DELETE /auth/account per account to trigger Kubo unpin) — deferred until after fix validation
Investigate per-upload someguy calls (#3): agent found 2 someguy PUTs per upload; per-file IPNS publish at seq-1 is prime deferral candidate — findings not yet acted on
Consider upgrading staging to ≥4 vCPU Hostinger plan — current 2-core ceiling limits ipfs+someguy combined throughput; at 4 cores the cpus=1.5 + roots changes should recover toward 15 ops/s
Commit fresh load-test baselines from the 7-run sweep and post-GC/post-fix runs to tests/load/baselines/ — still using stale March 2026 anchors
Recalibrate createFolder threshold in thresholds.ts to be concurrency-scaled (5000ms is too tight at 50+ clients) and add a moveItem threshold
Add sdk-folder-read, sdk-ipns-contention scenarios to the load-test.yml workflow dispatch dropdown to enable read-path regression testing against staging
The temporary VPS compose edit (ipfs memory 3G) and `docker update` CPU cap (1.5) are now permanent via the PR but the VPS will only pick them up on next deploy — verify after next staging deploy
Volume snapshot at /opt/cipherbox/ipfs_staging.backup.pre042.tar is temporary and should be cleaned up after confirming v0.42.0 stability on staging
